prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a new temple was dedicated in 1984 (not rededications).
prompts.text_original: A country where a new temple was dedicated in 1984 (not counting rededications).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (original dedication dates), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: In 1984 new temples were dedicated in Asia, the Pacific and Latin America as well as the United States. Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated Sydney Australia, Manila Philippines, Taipei Taiwan and Guatemala City Guatemala that year, and Boise Idaho and Dallas Texas were also dedicated.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Boise Idaho; Dallas Texas (dedicated 1984).

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Sydney Australia (dedicated 1984).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Manila Philippines (dedicated 1984).

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Guatemala City Guatemala (dedicated 1984).

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Taipei Taiwan (dedicated 1984).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was announced in 2019 or 2020.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was announced in 2019 or 2020.
prompts.note: Hong Kong, which has had a temple since 1996, is counted separately from mainland China.
prompts.summary: In 2019 and 2020 eight countries and territories got their first temple announcement, including Hungary, Sierra Leone, Papua New Guinea, Kiribati and China (Shanghai). As of October 2026 none of the eight is dedicated yet; most are under construction.

answers.name: People's Republic of China
answers.fact: Shanghai, announced 2020.

answers.name: United Arab Emirates
answers.fact: Dubai United Arab Emirates, announced 2020.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Budapest Hungary, announced 2019.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Pago Pago American Samoa, announced 2019.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: Tarawa Kiribati, announced 2020.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: Port Moresby Papua New Guinea, announced 2019.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: Freetown Sierra Leone, announced 2019.

answers.name: Vanuatu
answers.fact: Port Vila Vanuatu, announced 2020.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that was home to a foreign god named in the Old Testament, from Chemosh to Dagon
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding the home city or land of a foreign god named in the Old Testament: Chemosh of Moab, Milcom of Ammon, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Dagon of Ashdod and Gaza, Baal-zebub of Ekron, Rimmon of Damascus, Ashima of Hamath, Nisroch of Nineveh, Nergal of Cuth, Bel and Nebo of Babylon, and the gods of Egypt
prompts.citation: 1 Samuel 5; 1 Kings 11; 2 Kings 1, 5, 17, 19; Judges 16; Isaiah 46; Exodus 12
prompts.note: Gaza is in Palestine; Ashdod and Ekron are in Israel.
prompts.summary: The Old Testament names many gods of Israel's neighbours: Chemosh of Moab, Milcom of Ammon, Ashtoreth of Zidon, Dagon of the Philistines, Rimmon of Damascus and Nisroch of Nineveh. The ark toppled Dagon's image at Ashdod, Samson pulled down Dagon's house at Gaza, and Isaiah mocked Bel and Nebo of Babylon (1 Sam 5; Judg 16; Isa 46).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The Lord said he would execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt (Ex 12:12).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Chemosh was the abomination of Moab and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites (1 Kgs 11:5, 7).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians (1 Kgs 11:5).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Sennacherib was slain worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god at Nineveh; Bel and Nebo were gods of Babylon (2 Kgs 19:36-37; Isa 46:1).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The Philistines set the ark in the house of Dagon at Ashdod, and Baal-zebub was the god of Ekron (1 Sam 5:2; 2 Kgs 1:2).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Naaman's master worshipped in the house of Rimmon at Damascus, and the men of Hamath made Ashima (2 Kgs 5:18; 17:30).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The lords of the Philistines gathered at Gaza to sacrifice to Dagon when Samson was captured (Judg 16:21-23).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a kingdom or battle site in the war of the kings, Genesis 14
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a kingdom or battle site in the war of the kings in Genesis 14: the eastern kings of Shinar and Elam, the peoples they smote from Ashteroth Karnaim to mount Seir and El-paran, the vale of Siddim by the salt sea, and Abram's pursuit to Dan and Hobah near Damascus
prompts.note: The salt sea (Dead Sea) is shared by Israel, Jordan and the West Bank, so all three count for the vale of Siddim.
prompts.summary: Four eastern kings led by Chedorlaomer of Elam crushed a revolt by five cities of the plain, swept through Bashan, Moab, Seir and Kadesh, and carried Lot away from Sodom. Abram armed 318 servants, pursued them to Dan and beyond Damascus, rescued Lot, and paid tithes to Melchizedek king of Salem (Gen 14).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Amraphel was king of Shinar, the land of Babylon (Gen 14:1).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The kings smote the Amorites at Hazezon-tamar, which is Engedi, and Abram pursued them unto Dan (Gen 14:7, 14; 2 Chr 20:2).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Chedorlaomer, who led the war, was king of Elam (Gen 14:1, 4-5).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: They smote the Zuzims in Ham and the Horites in their mount Seir (Gen 14:5-6).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: They smote the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, and Abram chased them to Hobah, on the left hand of Damascus (Gen 14:5, 15).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The Horites were smitten in mount Seir unto El-paran, the wilderness of Paran in the central Sinai peninsula (Gen 14:6; Bible Dictionary, Paran).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The battle was in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt sea (Gen 14:3); the Dead Sea's northwest shore is in the West Bank.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Orson Hyde stopped on his 1841 trip to dedicate the Holy Land (marked map stops).
prompts.text_original: A country holding a city where Orson Hyde stopped on his 1841 mission journey from London to Jerusalem and back to Trieste, as mapped by the Joseph Smith Papers (Jerusalem itself not counted).
prompts.citation: Joseph Smith Papers map, Orson Hyde's mission travels June-December 1841; Saints vol. 1 ch. 36
prompts.note: Only the cities marked on the JSP map count. The Danube leg (Austria, Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania) has no marked stops.
prompts.summary: In 1840 Orson Hyde saw London, Amsterdam, Constantinople and Jerusalem in vision and was sent to dedicate the Holy Land. He crossed Europe, sailed by way of Smyrna and Beirut to Jaffa, and prayed on the Mount of Olives on October 24, 1841. He returned through Egypt, Trieste and Germany and reached Nauvoo in December 1842.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London, where he departed in June 1841 after helping the Twelve in England.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jaffa, where he landed in October 1841 before going inland to Jerusalem.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Mainz, Frankfurt and Regensburg, where he boarded a Danube steamer in August 1841.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Damietta, Cairo and Alexandria on the way home, November 1841.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Constantinople (Istanbul) and Smyrna (Izmir).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Beirut, on the sea route from Smyrna to Jaffa.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Arnhem.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Trieste, then Austrian and now in Italy, reached in December 1841.
